newsitem.title: UK: Specials still in demand on UK gilt repo market.
newsitem.headline: Specials still in demand on UK gilt repo market.

text.p: A handful of special stocks again deominated business on the UK gilt repo market, with the 8.0 percent gilts due 2003 trading nearly 300 basis points below general collateral (GC) levels.
The cash market had a comfortable day, with overnight cash ending at around 5.0 percent.
Repo traders there was continued good demand for the 8.0s of 2003, which traded overnight at around 2.75 percent.
Other specials included the 6.0s of 1999, 7.0s of 2001 and 6.75s of 2004, with the latter around 20 points below GC.
The Bank of England said the stock to be offered at the September 25 gilt auction would, as expected, be three billion stg of 8.0 percent gilts due 2021.
But this failed to generate much interest today in the existing stock, which traders said was in line with GC.
"There was not a lot going on, mostly short dates out to one month," one trader said.
Cash traders expressed surprise that they had enjoyed a second comfortable day in a row, with a modest 850 million stg shortage largely taken out.
"There is enough short paper around and people are happy to release it, given that cheaper official rates are unlikely in the very near future," a trader at a discount house said.
The Bank of England will make its fortnightly repo offer on Wednesday and traders said shortages could rise if it is not fully taken up.

"Maybe if we get less done on the gilt repo, the shortages will be slightly larger and we'll be back to a slightly firmer picture," one trader said. "But at the moment it all looks quite comfortable at the short end."
Late quotes for overnight cash dipped close to 4.0 percent but 5.0 percent was seen as a general closing level.
